calls.text: Consensus Strong Buy across 49 analysts; average target $1,560.57 (+57.8% vs the Oct 12 close)

bull.text: FY26 revenue +256% with ~81% gross margin and $59B of free cash flow

Forward P/E ~6× with Street targeting ~$1,555 (~43% upside)

news.title: Micron falls 6.3% as Tesla's capex cut, Lam's forecast and AI-funding worries hit chips
news.summary: Micron closed down 6.3% in a sector-wide selloff along with Intel and AMD (about −8%), Nvidia (−4.4%) and Sandisk (−8.5%). The Taoyuan union's 24-hour symbolic strike ran until 9 a.m. Friday Taiwan time with no confirmed production disruption; Micron Taiwan said the Taichung deal adds a quarterly profit-sharing bonus.

news.title: Micron Taoyuan union officials begin a 24-hour symbolic strike after a deal with the Taichung union
news.summary: Eleven Taoyuan union officials began a one-day strike at 9 a.m. Thursday that the union said is not meant to disrupt production. Micron signed an agreement with the larger Taichung union on Oct. 21 (terms undisclosed); Taoyuan talks resume Friday. The union seeks 15% of operating profit for profit-sharing.

news.title: Micron reaches a deal with its Taichung union, but Taoyuan union proceeds with a strike
news.summary: TrendForce said Taoyuan focuses on front-end DRAM wafers while Taichung makes advanced DRAM and HBM; if the action lasts only a day and critical production stays normal, the supply impact would likely be limited.

news.title: Micron faces a planned strike at its Taoyuan, Taiwan site on Thursday, Oct. 22
news.summary: The Taoyuan union, seeking a bonus plan worth 15% of operating profit, said 1,994 members (99% of those voting) backed strike action in support of workers at Micron's Taichung site. The length of the walkout is unclear.

news.title: Micron invests in Indium Corporation's New York critical-minerals processing
news.summary: Strategic funding under Micron's up-to-$3B US supply-chain plan will expand Indium's refining and manufacturing in Rome, N.Y., with a long-term supply agreement giving Micron access to high-purity minerals for advanced memory.

news.title: Micron closes up 3% at $904.90 as dip buyers return to memory stocks
news.summary: Micron rose as much as 4.2% after shedding about 11% last week on AI-spending and CXMT competition worries; COO Manish Bhatia recently said 2027 capacity at the Taichung fab is sold out. Its Taoyuan union has secured the legal right to strike after an 88.3% vote, though no strike has been called; a Taichung mediation session is set for Oct. 22.

news.title: Micron rises 2.5% premarket after last week's memory selloff
news.summary: MU traded at $900.78 early Monday (+2.5%) as futures rebounded and oil fell. A report, not confirmed by the companies, says Nvidia asked Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung to use TSMC's 3nm process for next-generation HBM base dies; competition worries from China's CXMT remain.

news.title: Micron is down 30% from its high and back below $1 trillion
news.summary: MU's 5.63% drop to $878.84 left it worth $994.34B, nearly 30% below its $1,255 52-week high, after falls in six of seven sessions since Oct. 7 (−19.2%). The average analyst target of $1,560.57 implies about 77.6% upside; management says over 75% of 2027 output is already committed.

news.title: Micron drops 5.6% to $878.84 on CXMT competition fears and the AI selloff
news.summary: MU traded as low as $875 as worries grew that China's CXMT is advancing in DDR5, LPDDR5X and server memory; AMD fell 6%, Intel 5.8% and Broadcom 4.5% on the day (AP). Bernstein's Mark Newman said he sees value in memory stocks after the pullback.

news.title: Micron snaps a three-day slide, rising 1.9% to $931
news.summary: MU turned positive during the session after opening near $872, helped by ASML saying its capacity is booked through 2028; China's CXMT remains the main overhang after SK Hynix fell 11% and Samsung 10% in Seoul. MarketBeat's consensus is Moderate Buy with a $1,407.88 average target.

news.title: Micron drops another 4.1% to $914 on CXMT competition fears and hot CPI
news.summary: MU fell for a third straight day, closing at $914.13 (about 13% off last week's levels), as China's CXMT touted a denser 4F-square server DRAM design and inflation data hit chip stocks. Consensus remains Moderate Buy; Micron has signed 26 long-term customer agreements covering more than 75% of expected fiscal-2027 output.

news.title: Micron extends its slide as Netlist's ITC patent cases weigh on the memory trade
news.summary: Netlist is seeking U.S. import exclusion orders at the ITC over Micron's HBM3E/HBM4/HBM4E lines, and a separate ITC probe covers Micron DDR5 server modules (also naming Supermicro, HPE and Lenovo). Combined with CXMT's DRAM news, MU closed down 3.6% at $953.19, about 7% below Friday's close.

listContext.method: Conservative growth at a reasonable price (GARP), rerun on the full US-listed market (StockAnalysis / S&P Global screener, Oct 23, 2026 close). A stock qualifies if it has: market cap of $10B or more and at least a year of trading history; TTM revenue growth of 15% or more that analysts expect to continue (consensus revenue growth of 8%+ next fiscal year and 8%+ a year over the next 3 years); a positive forward P/E of 35 or less and a PEG of 1.5 or less where available; a Buy or Strong Buy consensus from 5+ analysts with 15%+ upside to the average target; beta of 2.6 or less; share count up no
